title: Text and accessibility

location.series: City of Helsinki live visual identity guidelines

slide_intent: Make contrast and hierarchy explicit because readers need to distinguish information levels and read the words themselves.
strategic_value: Clear type hierarchy can make Helsinki communication usable across services and viewing situations.
demonstration: This expanded webpage section presents text-only guidance on size, color contrast, sign text and distinct heading/body/caption roles.
practical_value: Check contrast and separate type roles before evaluating decorative expression.

content_islands.name: Readability guidance
content_islands.spec: Place size, contrast and sign-color instructions first.

content_islands.name: Hierarchy guidance
content_islands.spec: Follow with the requirement to distinguish titles, subheadings, body and captions.

ingredient.name: Readable text hierarchy
ingredient.role: Make information levels identifiable and text legible.
ingredient.application: Use sufficient size/contrast and clearly separate title, subheading, body and caption roles.
ingredient.scope: The black-or-white text restriction here applies specifically to signs, not every city communication.

reference_purposes.Intent: The source explicitly connects adequate size and contrast to readability and clear hierarchy to accessibility.
reference_purposes.Application: It identifies four text roles that must be clearly separated.
reference_purposes.Constraint: Signs always use black or white text; light text on light/white backgrounds is rejected.
